question: Does the AC1024 aerial drawing's SUN owner failure reflect a local owner-resolution bug, or does independent decoding confirm that its hard-owner and common-owner edges disagree?

source.fixturePolicy: Existing local investigation input; not added to or modified in the repository.

localReader.diagnostic: DXF export preflight failed: SUN owner graph closure: SUN parent mismatch: owner 0x242, SUN 0x24c, parent 0x246
localReader.readDisposition: 337/337 source frames published; zero entity or object parse failures. Output stopped in preparation before publication.

observations: VIEW 0x242 has Sun handle 0x24c and the DWG reader decodes its field as group 361, hard owner.
XRECORD 0x246 is an entry named ADSK_XREC_VTRVIEWINFO in VIEW 0x242's extension dictionary 0x245; it is not the VIEW object itself.
The NOD has no ACAD_SUN root in this source, so the separately qualified dictionary-owner route does not apply.

authoritativeFormatEvidence.rule: The VIEW Sun handle is group 361 and is a hard-owner reference.
authoritativeFormatEvidence.interpretation: The decoded VIEW hard-owner target and SUN common owner do not identify the same object. The extension-dictionary XRECORD does not repair that mismatch under the documented VIEW ownership edge.

decision: Keep this SUN route refused. Do not infer or synthesize an owner edge from the extension-dictionary XRECORD. A different producer-backed graph with reciprocal VIEW/SUN ownership may qualify independently.
scopeLimits: This is one physical AC1024 source and does not establish that all SUN graphs are malformed.
LibreDWG parsing corroborates object identities and handles but is not native rendering evidence.
